How much does supply and fit cost? Supply-and-fit costs vary by condition type: Used £2,500-£4,500, Reconditioned £3,500-£5,500, Rebuilt £4,500-£7,500, Remanufactured £5,500-£9,000. Labour is the biggest variable - regional rates range from £65-£160/hr. What's included in the fitting cost? Fitting typically includes: removal of the old engine, installation of the replacement engine, new consumables (oil, coolant, filters), basic gaskets and seals, post-installation testing, and disposal of the old engine. Always get a written breakdown. How long does engine replacement take? The average timeline from quote request to completion is 5.2 days [EM-VERIFIED]. Labour typically takes 8-15 hours depending on engine type and vehicle complexity. What warranty comes with supply and fit? The warranty depends on the condition type: Used 1-6 months (parts only), Reconditioned 6-12 months (parts & labour), Rebuilt 12-24 months (parts & labour), Remanufactured 12-24 months (parts & labour). Do you offer vehicle recovery? Some suppliers offer recovery as part of the service. If not, you can arrange independent recovery or use your breakdown cover. We recommend confirming recovery options when you get your quotes. Can I choose my own garage? If you choose supply-only, you can use any garage. If you choose supply-and-fit, the supplier will arrange fitting with one of their partner garages. What if I already have my own garage? You can choose supply-only and have the engine delivered to your chosen garage. The supplier will provide the engine; your garage handles the fitting. Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer? DVLA - update the engine number on your V5C registration document [DVLA, 2025]. Insurer - you should check with your insurer to ensure proper policy coverage after major mechanical replacements. sections.heading: Signs You Need a Complete Engine Replacement

blocks.text: Before committing to a supply-and-fit engine replacement, check if your symptoms indicate terminal failure:
🔊 Deep knocking or rumbling from engine
Rod bearing or main bearing failure - bottom-end damage is usually terminal.
Catastrophic internal failure - no oil pressure, rod through block - engine is scrap.
⛓️ Snapped timing belt/chain on interference engine
Valves have hit pistons - extensive damage. Repair often costs more than replacement.
Spun bearing, damaged crankshaft, debris in oil system - destroys the block.
Head gasket failure, cracked block or cylinder head - may be repairable if caught early.
Internal wear - bearings, rings, cylinder bores - internal damage is widespread.

"Most of the engines we replace are beyond economic repair. When you're looking at a snapped timing chain, a spun bearing, or a seized engine, the cost of repair often exceeds the cost of replacement - and you still don't know what else is damaged inside. Supply-and-fit gives you a clean slate."
